title.narrative: Enhancing Nutrition Services for Under-5s and Pregnant/Breastfeeding Women in Bama, Dikwa, and Monguno LGAs, Borno State

description.narrative: ltpgtProtection Without Borders (POWIB) proposes a six-month intervention titled “Life-Saving Preventive and Curative Nutrition Assistance for Children under 5 and Pregnant Breastfeeding Women and Girls in Bama, Dikwa and Monguno LGAs, Borno State.” The project aims to reach approximately 7,950 individuals, prioritizing the most vulnerable populations—especially women and children—in three LGAs identified by the Nutrition Sector’s 2025 Lean Season Response Plan as having among the highest projected burdens of acute malnutrition. All nutrition services will be delivered through existing government health facilities and community structures to ensure sustainability.ltbrgtDrawing on POWIB’s extensive experience in Nutrition, Protection, and Cash-based programming, the intervention adopts an integrated approach that tackles both the immediate and structural drivers of malnutrition. It combines the Integrated Management of Acute Malnutrition (IMAM) with Maternal, Infant and Young Child Nutrition (MIYCN) counselling, Gender-Based Violence (GBV) and Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) awareness, and Cash and Voucher Assistance (CVA) to holistically respond to the nutrition crisis.ltbrgtPOWIB (Lead Partner) will implement the curative nutrition component across Bama, Dikwa, and Monguno LGAs, establishing and supporting Outpatient Therapeutic Programme (OTP) sites to ensure early identification and treatment of Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) and Moderate Acute Malnutrition (MAM) among children under five, as well as treatment of Pregnant and Breastfeeding Women and Girls (PBWG) with acute malnutrition. At least 2,100 children with SAM will receive Ready-to-Use Therapeutic Foods (RUTF), while 1,050 children with MAM and 215 PBWG will benefit from supplementary feeding. CVA will enable vulnerable households to sustain adherence to treatment and maintain dietary diversity.ltbrgtIn addition, POWIB will lead the preventive nutrition component in Monguno LGA, delivering MIYCN counselling, cooking demonstrations, IYCF support groups, and hygiene promotion integrated with protection messaging and GBV/PSEA awareness.ltbrgtGodiya Cherished Care for Humanitarian Response Initiative (GCCHRI) will serve as the sole sub-grantee, implementing the preventive nutrition component in Bama and Dikwa LGAs. GCCHRI will conduct MIYCN counselling, establish and mentor Mother-to-Mother and Father-to-Father Support Groups, organize cooking demonstrations, promote hygiene practices, and integrate GBV/PSEA sensitization and referral systems to strengthen community protection mechanisms.ltbrgtThe consortium will collaborate closely with the Borno State Primary Health Care Development Agency (BSPHCDA), community leaders, and sector partners to ensure coordination, referrals, and sustainability. At least 60 health workers and community nutrition mobilizers will be trained and mentored across the three LGAs to strengthen service delivery and local ownership.ltbrgtBy integrating curative nutrition, preventive care, protection mainstreaming, and cash assistance, the project simultaneously addresses lifesaving needs and the underlying vulnerabilities driving malnutrition. It aligns with the Nutrition Sector priorities, the National Multisectoral Plan of Action for Food and Nutrition, and contributes to the Sustainable Development Goals. To ensure effective delivery and sustainability, POWIB will continue to strengthen partner capacity through tailored training, mentorship, provision of tools, joint coordination with government systems, and improved data use—enhancing service quality, localization, and long-term impact across Bama, Dikwa, and Monguno LGAs.ltbrgtlt/pgt
